label: Plane Geometry
overview: Plane geometry covers angles, parallel lines, transversals, triangles, quadrilaterals, and polygons. Key angle relationships: vertical angles are equal, supplementary angles sum to 180°, and angles in a triangle sum to 180°. For parallel lines cut by a transversal, corresponding, alternate interior, and co-interior (same-side interior) angles have predictable relationships.

keyFormulas.name: Exterior angle theorem
keyFormulas.latex: \text{exterior angle} = \text{sum of two non-adjacent interior angles}

workedExamples.problem: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One angle is (3x + 20)° and its alternate interior angle is (5x − 40)°. Find x.

steps.title: Use the alternate interior angles theorem
steps.content: Alternate interior angles formed by parallel lines are equal.

commonMistakes.mistake: Confusing co-interior (same-side interior) angles as equal when they are actually supplementary
commonMistakes.fix: Alternate interior angles (on opposite sides of the transversal) are equal. Co-interior angles (same side) add to 180°.

commonMistakes.mistake: Applying the triangle angle sum to a quadrilateral
commonMistakes.fix: Use (n−2) × 180° for any polygon. For a triangle n=3 → 180°. For a quadrilateral n=4 → 360°.

quickTip: Mark all angle relationships on the diagram before writing equations. Visual organisation prevents mixing up which angles are equal vs. supplementary.
